SIMULATION PLAN (no live Notion writes executed)

1. PROCEED NOW: Create the operational note (independent verified operation)
- Pre-check: Search Notes & References for an existing matching note before creating; reuse only if an exact entity match exists.
- Create operation: Create a page in Notes & References using the verified blank default template T (do not create or alter templates).
- Native properties to set:
  - Name (title): Concise title for the note (e.g., "Interview response rate drop")
  - Type (select): Note
  - Project (relation): verified page ID/URL for launch
  - Area (relation): verified page ID/URL for marketing
  - Leave managed/read-only fields (Created Time, Last Edited Time) untouched; do not invent Date, Status, Tags, or Summary.
- Exact page body:
  Interview response rate fell this week.
  (Keep Project and Area strictly in native properties; do not mirror or list Project/Area metadata in the body.)
- Post-write verification:
  - Confirm asynchronous template T application completed without overwriting supplied properties or body.
  - Re-read the persisted page by ID to verify Name, Type, native Project=launch, native Area=marketing (plus reciprocal Notes links on launch and marketing without issuing competing writes), and exact body text.

2. HOLD ONLY THE DEPENDENT TASK RELATION WRITE (changed target + has_more=true)
- Hold: Do not write the changed relation on the other task yet. Do not select a target from a truncated page, rely on the stale snapshot, or claim absence/uniqueness while has_more=true.
- Required verification before writing:
  1. Fetch the live schema for that task's relation property to confirm the current target database, property type, and meaning.
  2. Exhaust pagination by following cursors until has_more=false.
  3. Resolve the exact live target page ID/URL and verify compatibility (no self-link, transitive cycle, or conflicting Project/Stage context).
  4. Write the relation using the verified live ID and re-read to confirm persisted state.
- Independent work (the operational note above) proceeds without waiting on this hold.

3. DONE PREDECESSOR, RETAINED HISTORY LINK, AND NEXT ACTIONS VISIBILITY WARNING
- Preserved state (no implicit edits):
  - Retain the historical Blocked by link to the Done predecessor; do not delete dependency history.
  - Do not modify the Next Actions view filter or schema (outside bounded record authorization).
  - Do not certify the successor as executable from predecessor closure alone until all other potential blockers on that successor are checked.
- Visibility warning:
  - Because the current Next Actions view filters for an empty Blocked by relation, keeping the historical link to the Done predecessor keeps the successor hidden from Next Actions even if it has Next Action status and no remaining open blockers.
- Scoped options requiring your explicit decision:
  1. Keep both the history link and current view unchanged for the review and inspect the successor directly outside Next Actions.
  2. Explicitly authorize a structural view-filter update on Next Actions (inspecting source and dashboard views and verifying saved filter operators) so it filters by unresolved blockers rather than empty Blocked by.
  3. Explicitly specify another record-level handling if you intentionally want a different trade-off.
